citation.title: A Gaussian process guide for signal regression in magnetic fusion
citation.authors: Michoski C., Oliver T.A., Hatch D.R., Diallo A., Kotschenreuther M., Eldon D., Waller M., Groebner R., Nelson A.O.

topic: Offline GPR fitting of DIII-D edge Thomson-scattering Te profiles; hyperparameter and prior-mean sensitivity
own_question: How to apply GPR in a principled way to pedestal Te profile fitting, and which pitfalls (pooling, kernel, hyperparameters, prior mean) affect interpretation.
actual_method_and_evidence: Discretized GP with an RBF kernel and a monotonicity-promoting prior on dTe/dpsi. Fits to one DIII-D H-mode discharge (#153764), comparing ELM-pooled data with a single profile. Uses a Gamma-function credibility metric, MLE/MAP and emcee marginalization over (sigma, l), and three prior means. Pooled fits had credibility near zero. Single-profile fits were credible but sensitive to l, sigma and prior mean (Table 2).

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: GPR has been used offline to fit tokamak edge electron-temperature profiles with uncertainty. Its conclusions depend on kernel hyperparameters and the prior mean.
claim_checks.qualification: One DIII-D discharge; spatial profile regression of Thomson Te. Not temporal and not ion/impurity CES.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: A posterior GP conditioned on Gaussian noisy observations has closed-form mean and covariance. This is background for a causal GP baseline.
claim_checks.qualification: Standard textbook result, restated here. No causal or time-series use is shown in this paper.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Spatial inputs: normalized psi with Thomson Te pooled over 80-99% of the ELM cycle, or a single profile. No time-causal setting. No real-time computation or timing is reported.
validation_if_relevant: Credibility (Bayesian p-value) against the fitted data only. No held-out data. Pooled versus single-profile fits are compared within one discharge.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite this as evidence for CES impurity Ti or for nowcasting.
Do not cite it as demonstrating real-time GP feasibility.
Do not use it to say prior GP work is generally noncausal.
Do not treat its monotonicity prior or MTM length-scale reasoning as validated physics.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Useful supporting citation for GP background and hyperparameter/prior sensitivity, which is relevant to our causalGP baseline. It differs in diagnostic, species, dimension and timing.
